payload.summary: The pinned repository (angus924/rocket @ 36bd908b, the official ROCKET authors' repo, linked from the paper's arXiv/DMKD reference) contains official code matching the claimed method: rocket_functions.py implements generate_kernels (random dilated convolutional kernels, default 10,000) and apply_kernels (PPV and max features), and code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py runs the UCR protocol with RidgeClassifierCV(alphas=logspace(-3,3,10), normalize=True), using the fixed _TRAIN/_TEST split and 10 runs by default, reporting mean test accuracy per dataset. ECG200 is in the bake-off list in .preprint/reproduce_experiments_bakeoff.py and appears in results/results_ucr.csv and results/results_ucr_resamples.csv. The claim's method, dataset, split, and metric are therefore all covered by official code. No dependency file exists in the repo (dependency_discover found none); the README lists Python, Numba, NumPy and scikit-learn as requirements. Saved notebook outputs were removed, so the metric must be recomputed by running the script.

entrypoints.why: Official UCR experiment script: loads {input}/{name}/{name}_TRAIN.txt and _TEST.txt, runs 10 kernel-generation runs (default -k 10000), fits RidgeClassifierCV, and writes mean and std test accuracy to results_ucr.csv. Requires -d (dataset list txt), -i, -o.
Core ROCKET implementation: generate_kernels and apply_kernels (numba-jitted), used by the UCR script and the README example.
Preprint-era bake-off script with the 85-dataset list including ECG200; same ROCKET pipeline with 10 runs and 10,000 kernels by default.

dataFiles.why: Not a data file; it expects external UCR data at {input_path}/ECG200/ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200_TEST.txt (timeseriesclassification.com Univariate_arff txt version). The data is not bundled in the repository.

metricSources.description: Computes per-run test accuracy via classifier.score(X_test_transform, Y_test) and the mean across runs (accuracy_mean); written to results_ucr.csv. This is the metric the claim refers to.
Saved output of the UCR script; ECG200 row holds the mean accuracy from the repository's own run (not reported here).
Resample-based results file; ECG200 row present. Reference only, not the fixed split.

payload.runInstructions: Install Python with numpy, pandas, numba, and scikit-learn (no pinned versions in repo; the code uses np.NINF and RidgeClassifierCV(normalize=...), so older scikit-learn versions (<1.2) are likely needed). Download UCR Univariate_arff txt data (timeseriesclassification.com, 2018 version) so that ECG200/ECG200_TRAIN.txt and ECG200/ECG200_TEST.txt exist under an input directory. Create a file ecg200.txt containing the line ECG200. Run: python code/reproduce_experiments_ucr.py -d ecg200.txt -i <input_dir> -o <output_dir> -n 10 -k 10000 (run from the code/ directory so rocket_functions imports). The output accuracy_mean for ECG200 is the claimed metric. Note that the kernel generation is random (np.random without seed), so run-to-run variance is expected.

No command ran, no artifacts/result.json was produced, no metric was observed, and no blind review was performed. The paper value (0.9272) cannot be compared against anything, so neither reproduction nor non-reproduction can be claimed. The computed status 'inconclusive' is the correct, appropriately cautious outcome. A replan that routes the run through the declared adapter with a reviewed hash could be attempted, but that is a new attempt rather than evidence for this run.
